name: Drought
value: El Niño drought threat; no crop failure
summary: Super El Niño threatens drought in southern Africa and Asia; no major exporter's harvest has failed
state: Forecasters warn the strong El Niño threatens southern Africa with drought and lower maize harvests, and WFP has warned that millions could face hunger (CITE; Briefly News). South Africa's summer grain crop is at risk, though earlier rains and grain stocks offer some cushion (Down To Earth). No harvest failure in a major exporter had been confirmed as of 7 Nov.
for_you: Drought tends to raise local food prices first; global grain prices react if exporters' harvests fail.
rubric_hit: Severe drought threat in major crop regions = Watch; no exporter harvest failure (Alert)

sources.title: CITE — Super El Niño threatens southern Africa with drought and crop failures
Down To Earth — Will El Niño drought hit food prices in South Africa?

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
